title: The Schedule Waters Regardless, Explained
subtitle: Casimir Beng, Mirela Hanke and Joost Nwosu on testing the central quad’s occupancy-aware sprinklers against a term of pedestrian counts
summary: A research explainer from the School of Continuous Improvement on Casimir Beng, Mirela Hanke and Joost Nwosu’s validation study of the central quad’s occupancy-aware irrigation controller. It follows the lawn’s busiest zone through seven weeks of independent pedestrian counts and a fortnight with the sensor unplugged, and sets the controller’s watering beside the crowd it was installed to notice. The three authors describe the work in their own words.
topic: A research explainer of the validation study testing whether the central quad’s occupancy-aware irrigation controller responds to independently counted foot traffic or repeats its fixed timetable, from seven weeks of pedestrian counts across four irrigation zones and a two-week sensor-disconnection ablation, which found no measurable relationship between occupancy and suppression and no change in watering with the sensor removed

beats.text: A smart label is often a promise, not a demonstrated property.
Every occupancy-aware system we operate is going to need this check eventually. We’d rather run it ourselves, on our own lawn, than wait for someone else to ask.
